personae.name: Magnificoes of Venice
personae.blurb: Officers of the Court of Justice, a Gaoler, Servants and other Attendants

lines.text: Enter Antonio, Salarino and Solanio.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: In sooth I know not why I am so sad,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: It wearies me, you say it wearies you;

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: But how I caught it, found it, or came by it,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: What stuff ’tis made of, whereof it is born,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I am to learn.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: And such a want-wit sadness makes of me,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: That I have much ado to know myself.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Your mind is tossing on the ocean,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: There where your argosies, with portly sail

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Like signiors and rich burghers on the flood,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Or as it were the pageants of the sea,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Do overpeer the petty traffickers

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: That curtsy to them, do them reverence,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: As they fly by them with their woven wings.

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: Believe me, sir, had I such venture forth,

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: The better part of my affections would

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: Be with my hopes abroad. I should be still

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: Plucking the grass to know where sits the wind,

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: Peering in maps for ports, and piers and roads;

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: And every object that might make me fear

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: Misfortune to my ventures, out of doubt

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: Would make me sad.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: My wind cooling my broth

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Would blow me to an ague when I thought

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: What harm a wind too great might do at sea.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: I should not see the sandy hour-glass run

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: But I should think of shallows and of flats,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: And see my wealthy Andrew dock’d in sand,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Vailing her high top lower than her ribs

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: To kiss her burial. Should I go to church

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: And see the holy edifice of stone

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: And not bethink me straight of dangerous rocks,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Which, touching but my gentle vessel’s side,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Would scatter all her spices on the stream,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Enrobe the roaring waters with my silks,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: And, in a word, but even now worth this,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: And now worth nothing? Shall I have the thought

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: To think on this, and shall I lack the thought

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: That such a thing bechanc’d would make me sad?

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: But tell not me, I know Antonio

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Is sad to think upon his merchandise.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Believe me, no. I thank my fortune for it,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: My ventures are not in one bottom trusted,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Nor to one place; nor is my whole estate

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Upon the fortune of this present year.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Therefore my merchandise makes me not sad.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Why then you are in love.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Fie, fie!

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Not in love neither? Then let us say you are sad

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Because you are not merry; and ’twere as easy

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: For you to laugh and leap and say you are merry

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Because you are not sad. Now, by two-headed Janus,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Nature hath fram’d strange fellows in her time:

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Some that will evermore peep through their eyes,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: And laugh like parrots at a bagpiper.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: And other of such vinegar aspect

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: That they’ll not show their teeth in way of smile

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Though Nestor swear the jest be laughable.
Enter Bassanio, Lorenzo and Gratiano.

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: Here comes Bassanio, your most noble kinsman,

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: Gratiano, and Lorenzo. Fare ye well.

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: We leave you now with better company.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: I would have stay’d till I had made you merry,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: If worthier friends had not prevented me.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Your worth is very dear in my regard.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I take it your own business calls on you,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: And you embrace th’ occasion to depart.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Good morrow, my good lords.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Good signiors both, when shall we laugh? Say, when?

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: You grow exceeding strange. Must it be so?

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: We’ll make our leisures to attend on yours.
[_Exeunt Salarino and Solanio._]

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: My Lord Bassanio, since you have found Antonio,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: We two will leave you, but at dinner-time

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: I pray you have in mind where we must meet.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I will not fail you.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: You look not well, Signior Antonio,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: You have too much respect upon the world.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: They lose it that do buy it with much care.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Believe me, you are marvellously chang’d.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I hold the world but as the world, Gratiano,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: A stage, where every man must play a part,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: And mine a sad one.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Let me play the fool,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: With mirth and laughter let old wrinkles come,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: And let my liver rather heat with wine

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Than my heart cool with mortifying groans.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Why should a man whose blood is warm within

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Sit like his grandsire cut in alabaster?

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Sleep when he wakes? And creep into the jaundice

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: By being peevish? I tell thee what, Antonio,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: (I love thee, and ’tis my love that speaks):

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: There are a sort of men whose visages

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Do cream and mantle like a standing pond,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: And do a wilful stillness entertain,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: With purpose to be dress’d in an opinion

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Of wisdom, gravity, profound conceit,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: As who should say, “I am Sir Oracle,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: And when I ope my lips, let no dog bark.”

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: O my Antonio, I do know of these

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: That therefore only are reputed wise

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: For saying nothing; when, I am very sure,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: If they should speak, would almost damn those ears

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Which, hearing them, would call their brothers fools.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: I’ll tell thee more of this another time.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: But fish not with this melancholy bait

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: For this fool gudgeon, this opinion.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Come, good Lorenzo. Fare ye well a while.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: I’ll end my exhortation after dinner.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Well, we will leave you then till dinner-time.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: I must be one of these same dumb wise men,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: For Gratiano never lets me speak.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Well, keep me company but two years moe,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Thou shalt not know the sound of thine own tongue.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Fare you well. I’ll grow a talker for this gear.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Thanks, i’ faith, for silence is only commendable

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: In a neat’s tongue dried, and a maid not vendible.
[_Exeunt Gratiano and Lorenzo._]

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Is that anything now?

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Gratiano speaks an infinite deal of nothing, more than any man in all

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Venice. His reasons are as two grains of wheat hid in two bushels of

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: chaff: you shall seek all day ere you find them, and when you have them

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: they are not worth the search.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Well, tell me now what lady is the same

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: To whom you swore a secret pilgrimage,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: That you today promis’d to tell me of?

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: ’Tis not unknown to you, Antonio,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: How much I have disabled mine estate

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: By something showing a more swelling port

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Than my faint means would grant continuance.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Nor do I now make moan to be abridg’d

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: From such a noble rate, but my chief care

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Is to come fairly off from the great debts

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Wherein my time, something too prodigal,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Hath left me gag’d. To you, Antonio,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I owe the most in money and in love,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And from your love I have a warranty

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: To unburden all my plots and purposes

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: How to get clear of all the debts I owe.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I pray you, good Bassanio, let me know it;

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: And if it stand, as you yourself still do,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Within the eye of honour, be assur’d

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: My purse, my person, my extremest means

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Lie all unlock’d to your occasions.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: In my school-days, when I had lost one shaft,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I shot his fellow of the self-same flight

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: The self-same way, with more advised watch

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: To find the other forth; and by adventuring both

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I oft found both. I urge this childhood proof

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Because what follows is pure innocence.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I owe you much, and, like a wilful youth,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: That which I owe is lost. But if you please

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: To shoot another arrow that self way

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Which you did shoot the first, I do not doubt,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: As I will watch the aim, or to find both,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Or bring your latter hazard back again,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And thankfully rest debtor for the first.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: You know me well, and herein spend but time

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: To wind about my love with circumstance;

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: And out of doubt you do me now more wrong

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: In making question of my uttermost

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Than if you had made waste of all I have.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Then do but say to me what I should do

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: That in your knowledge may by me be done,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: And I am prest unto it. Therefore, speak.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: In Belmont is a lady richly left,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And she is fair, and, fairer than that word,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Of wondrous virtues. Sometimes from her eyes

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I did receive fair speechless messages:

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Her name is Portia, nothing undervalu’d

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: To Cato’s daughter, Brutus’ Portia.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Nor is the wide world ignorant of her worth,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: For the four winds blow in from every coast

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Renowned suitors, and her sunny locks

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Hang on her temples like a golden fleece,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Which makes her seat of Belmont Colchos’ strond,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And many Jasons come in quest of her.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: O my Antonio, had I but the means

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: To hold a rival place with one of them,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I have a mind presages me such thrift

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: That I should questionless be fortunate.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Thou know’st that all my fortunes are at sea;

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Neither have I money nor commodity

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: To raise a present sum, therefore go forth

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Try what my credit can in Venice do;

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: That shall be rack’d even to the uttermost,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: To furnish thee to Belmont to fair Portia.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Go presently inquire, and so will I,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Where money is, and I no question make

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: To have it of my trust or for my sake.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Belmont. A room in Portia’s house.

lines.text: Enter Portia with her waiting-woman Nerissa.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: By my troth, Nerissa, my little body is aweary of this great world.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: You would be, sweet madam, if your miseries were in the same abundance

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: as your good fortunes are. And yet, for aught I see, they are as sick

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: that surfeit with too much as they that starve with nothing. It is no

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: mean happiness, therefore, to be seated in the mean. Superfluity come

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: sooner by white hairs, but competency lives longer.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Good sentences, and well pronounc’d.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: They would be better if well followed.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: If to do were as easy as to know what were good to do, chapels had been

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: churches, and poor men’s cottages princes’ palaces. It is a good divine

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: that follows his own instructions; I can easier teach twenty what were

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: good to be done than to be one of the twenty to follow mine own

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: teaching. The brain may devise laws for the blood, but a hot temper

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: leaps o’er a cold decree; such a hare is madness the youth, to skip

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: o’er the meshes of good counsel the cripple. But this reasoning is not

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: in the fashion to choose me a husband. O me, the word “choose”! I may

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: neither choose who I would nor refuse who I dislike, so is the will of

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: a living daughter curb’d by the will of a dead father. Is it not hard,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Nerissa, that I cannot choose one, nor refuse none?

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: Your father was ever virtuous, and holy men at their death have good

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: inspirations. Therefore the lott’ry that he hath devised in these three

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: chests of gold, silver, and lead, whereof who chooses his meaning

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: chooses you, will no doubt never be chosen by any rightly but one who

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: you shall rightly love. But what warmth is there in your affection

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: towards any of these princely suitors that are already come?

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I pray thee over-name them, and as thou namest them, I will describe

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: them, and according to my description level at my affection.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: First, there is the Neapolitan prince.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Ay, that’s a colt indeed, for he doth nothing but talk of his horse,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: and he makes it a great appropriation to his own good parts that he can

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: shoe him himself. I am much afeard my lady his mother play’d false with

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: a smith.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: Then is there the County Palatine.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: He doth nothing but frown, as who should say “And you will not have me,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: choose.” He hears merry tales and smiles not. I fear he will prove the

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: weeping philosopher when he grows old, being so full of unmannerly

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: sadness in his youth. I had rather be married to a death’s-head with a

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: bone in his mouth than to either of these. God defend me from these

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: two!

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: How say you by the French lord, Monsieur Le Bon?

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: God made him, and therefore let him pass for a man. In truth, I know it

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: is a sin to be a mocker, but he! why, he hath a horse better than the

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Neapolitan’s, a better bad habit of frowning than the Count Palatine.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: He is every man in no man. If a throstle sing, he falls straight

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: a-cap’ring. He will fence with his own shadow. If I should marry him, I

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: should marry twenty husbands. If he would despise me, I would forgive

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: him, for if he love me to madness, I shall never requite him.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: What say you then to Falconbridge, the young baron of England?

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: You know I say nothing to him, for he understands not me, nor I him: he

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: hath neither Latin, French, nor Italian, and you will come into the

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: court and swear that I have a poor pennyworth in the English. He is a

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: proper man’s picture; but alas, who can converse with a dumb-show? How

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: oddly he is suited! I think he bought his doublet in Italy, his round

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: hose in France, his bonnet in Germany, and his behaviour everywhere.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: What think you of the Scottish lord, his neighbour?

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: That he hath a neighbourly charity in him, for he borrowed a box of the

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: ear of the Englishman, and swore he would pay him again when he was

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: able. I think the Frenchman became his surety, and seal’d under for

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: another.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: How like you the young German, the Duke of Saxony’s nephew?

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Very vilely in the morning when he is sober, and most vilely in the

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: afternoon when he is drunk: when he is best, he is a little worse than

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: a man, and when he is worst, he is little better than a beast. And the

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: worst fall that ever fell, I hope I shall make shift to go without him.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: If he should offer to choose, and choose the right casket, you should

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: refuse to perform your father’s will, if you should refuse to accept

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: him.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Therefore, for fear of the worst, I pray thee set a deep glass of

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Rhenish wine on the contrary casket, for if the devil be within and

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: that temptation without, I know he will choose it. I will do anything,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Nerissa, ere I will be married to a sponge.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: You need not fear, lady, the having any of these lords. They have

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: acquainted me with their determinations, which is indeed to return to

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: their home, and to trouble you with no more suit, unless you may be won

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: by some other sort than your father’s imposition, depending on the

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: caskets.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: If I live to be as old as Sibylla, I will die as chaste as Diana,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: unless I be obtained by the manner of my father’s will. I am glad this

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: parcel of wooers are so reasonable, for there is not one among them but

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I dote on his very absence. And I pray God grant them a fair departure.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: Do you not remember, lady, in your father’s time, a Venetian, a scholar

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: and a soldier, that came hither in company of the Marquis of

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: Montferrat?

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Yes, yes, it was Bassanio, as I think, so was he call’d.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: True, madam. He, of all the men that ever my foolish eyes look’d upon,

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: was the best deserving a fair lady.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I remember him well, and I remember him worthy of thy praise.
Enter a Servingman.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: How now! what news?

lines.speaker: SERVINGMAN
lines.text: The four strangers seek for you, madam, to take their leave. And there

lines.speaker: SERVINGMAN
lines.text: is a forerunner come from a fifth, the Prince of Morocco, who brings

lines.speaker: SERVINGMAN
lines.text: word the Prince his master will be here tonight.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: If I could bid the fifth welcome with so good heart as I can bid the

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: other four farewell, I should be glad of his approach. If he have the

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: condition of a saint and the complexion of a devil, I had rather he

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: should shrive me than wive me. Come, Nerissa. Sirrah, go before. Whiles

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: we shut the gate upon one wooer, another knocks at the door.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Bassanio with Shylock the Jew.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK

lines.text: his bond.

lines.text: If it please you to dine with us.

lines.text: He hates our sacred nation, and he rails,

lines.text: Of full three thousand ducats. What of that?

lines.text: Tubal, a wealthy Hebrew of my tribe,

lines.text: Do you desire? [_To Antonio._] Rest you fair, good signior,

lines.text: Shylock, albeit I neither lend nor borrow

lines.text: By taking nor by giving of excess,

lines.text: I’ll break a custom. [_To Bassanio._] Is he yet possess’d

lines.text: How much ye would?

lines.text: Ay, ay, three thousand ducats.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: And for three months.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: I had forgot, three months, you told me so.

lines.text: Well then, your bond. And let me see, but hear you,

lines.text: Methought you said you neither lend nor borrow

lines.text: Upon advantage.

lines.text: When Jacob graz’d his uncle Laban’s sheep,—

lines.text: This Jacob from our holy Abram was

lines.text: As his wise mother wrought in his behalf,

lines.text: And what of him? Did he take interest?

lines.text: No, not take interest, not, as you would say,

lines.text: When Laban and himself were compromis’d

lines.text: That all the eanlings which were streak’d and pied

lines.text: Should fall as Jacob’s hire, the ewes being rank

lines.text: In end of autumn turned to the rams,

lines.text: And when the work of generation was

lines.text: Between these woolly breeders in the act,

lines.text: The skilful shepherd pill’d me certain wands,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: And in the doing of the deed of kind,

lines.text: And thrift is blessing if men steal it not.

lines.text: This was a venture, sir, that Jacob serv’d for,

lines.text: But sway’d and fashion’d by the hand of heaven.

lines.text: Was this inserted to make interest good?

lines.text: Or is your gold and silver ewes and rams?

lines.text: I cannot tell; I make it breed as fast.

lines.text: But note me, signior.

lines.text: Mark you this, Bassanio,

lines.text: Three thousand ducats, ’tis a good round sum.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Three months from twelve, then let me see the rate.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Well, Shylock, shall we be beholding to you?

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Signior Antonio, many a time and oft

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: In the Rialto you have rated me

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: About my moneys and my usances.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Still have I borne it with a patient shrug,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: (For suff’rance is the badge of all our tribe.)

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: You call me misbeliever, cut-throat dog,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: And spet upon my Jewish gaberdine,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: And all for use of that which is mine own.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Well then, it now appears you need my help.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Go to, then, you come to me, and you say

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: “Shylock, we would have moneys.” You say so:

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: You that did void your rheum upon my beard,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: And foot me as you spurn a stranger cur

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Over your threshold, moneys is your suit.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: What should I say to you? Should I not say

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: “Hath a dog money? Is it possible

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: A cur can lend three thousand ducats?” Or

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Shall I bend low and, in a bondman’s key,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: With bated breath and whisp’ring humbleness,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Say this:

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: “Fair sir, you spet on me on Wednesday last;

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: You spurn’d me such a day; another time

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: You call’d me dog; and for these courtesies

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: I’ll lend you thus much moneys”?

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I am as like to call thee so again,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: To spet on thee again, to spurn thee too.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: If thou wilt lend this money, lend it not

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: As to thy friends, for when did friendship take

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: A breed for barren metal of his friend?

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: But lend it rather to thine enemy,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Who if he break, thou mayst with better face

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Exact the penalty.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Why, look you how you storm!

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: I would be friends with you, and have your love,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Forget the shames that you have stain’d me with,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Supply your present wants, and take no doit

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Of usance for my moneys, and you’ll not hear me,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: This is kind I offer.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: This were kindness.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: This kindness will I show.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Go with me to a notary, seal me there

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Your single bond; and in a merry sport,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: If you repay me not on such a day,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: In such a place, such sum or sums as are

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Express’d in the condition, let the forfeit

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Be nominated for an equal pound

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Of your fair flesh, to be cut off and taken

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: In what part of your body pleaseth me.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Content, in faith, I’ll seal to such a bond,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: And say there is much kindness in the Jew.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: You shall not seal to such a bond for me,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I’ll rather dwell in my necessity.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Why, fear not, man, I will not forfeit it,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Within these two months, that’s a month before

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: This bond expires, I do expect return

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Of thrice three times the value of this bond.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: O father Abram, what these Christians are,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Whose own hard dealings teaches them suspect

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: The thoughts of others. Pray you, tell me this,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: If he should break his day, what should I gain

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: By the exaction of the forfeiture?

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: A pound of man’s flesh, taken from a man,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Is not so estimable, profitable neither,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: As flesh of muttons, beefs, or goats. I say,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: To buy his favour, I extend this friendship.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: If he will take it, so. If not, adieu,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: And for my love I pray you wrong me not.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Yes, Shylock, I will seal unto this bond.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Then meet me forthwith at the notary’s,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Give him direction for this merry bond,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: And I will go and purse the ducats straight,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: See to my house left in the fearful guard

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Of an unthrifty knave, and presently

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: I’ll be with you.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO

lines.speaker: ANTONIO

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: Do you not know me, father?

lines.speaker: GOBBO
lines.text: Alack, sir, I am sand-blind, I know you not.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: Nay, indeed, if you had your eyes, you might fail of the knowing me: it

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: is a wise father that knows his own child. Well, old man, I will tell

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: you news of your son. Give me your blessing, truth will come to light,

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: murder cannot be hid long, a man’s son may, but in the end truth will

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: out.

lines.speaker: GOBBO
lines.text: Pray you, sir, stand up, I am sure you are not Launcelet my boy.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: Pray you, let’s have no more fooling about it, but give me your

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: blessing. I am Launcelet, your boy that was, your son that is, your

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: child that shall be.

lines.speaker: GOBBO
lines.text: I cannot think you are my son.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: I know not what I shall think of that; but I am Launcelet, the Jew’s

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: man, and I am sure Margery your wife is my mother.

lines.speaker: GOBBO
lines.text: Her name is Margery, indeed. I’ll be sworn if thou be Launcelet, thou

lines.speaker: GOBBO
lines.text: art mine own flesh and blood. Lord worshipped might he be, what a beard

lines.speaker: GOBBO
lines.text: hast thou got! Thou hast got more hair on thy chin than Dobbin my

lines.speaker: GOBBO
lines.text: fill-horse has on his tail.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: It should seem, then, that Dobbin’s tail grows backward. I am sure he

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: had more hair on his tail than I have on my face when I last saw him.

lines.speaker: GOBBO
lines.text: Lord, how art thou changed! How dost thou and thy master agree? I have

lines.speaker: GOBBO
lines.text: brought him a present. How ’gree you now?

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: Well, well. But for mine own part, as I have set up my rest to run

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: away, so I will not rest till I have run some ground. My master’s a

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: very Jew. Give him a present! Give him a halter. I am famished in his

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: service. You may tell every finger I have with my ribs. Father, I am

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: glad you are come, give me your present to one Master Bassanio, who

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: indeed gives rare new liveries. If I serve not him, I will run as far

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: as God has any ground. O rare fortune, here comes the man! To him,

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: father; for I am a Jew, if I serve the Jew any longer.
Enter Bassanio with Leonardo and a follower or two.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: You may do so, but let it be so hasted that supper be ready at the

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: farthest by five of the clock. See these letters delivered, put the

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: liveries to making, and desire Gratiano to come anon to my lodging.
[_Exit a Servant._]

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: To him, father.

lines.speaker: GOBBO
lines.text: God bless your worship!

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Gramercy, wouldst thou aught with me?

lines.speaker: GOBBO
lines.text: Here’s my son, sir, a poor boy.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: Not a poor boy, sir, but the rich Jew’s man, that would, sir, as my

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: father shall specify.

lines.speaker: GOBBO
lines.text: He hath a great infection, sir, as one would say, to serve.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: Indeed the short and the long is, I serve the Jew, and have a desire,

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: as my father shall specify.

lines.speaker: GOBBO
lines.text: His master and he (saving your worship’s reverence) are scarce

lines.speaker: GOBBO
lines.text: cater-cousins.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: To be brief, the very truth is that the Jew, having done me wrong, doth

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: cause me, as my father, being I hope an old man, shall frutify unto

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: you.

lines.speaker: GOBBO
lines.text: I have here a dish of doves that I would bestow upon your worship, and

lines.speaker: GOBBO
lines.text: my suit is—

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: In very brief, the suit is impertinent to myself, as your worship shall

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: know by this honest old man, and though I say it, though old man, yet

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: poor man, my father.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: One speak for both. What would you?

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: Serve you, sir.

lines.speaker: GOBBO
lines.text: That is the very defect of the matter, sir.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I know thee well; thou hast obtain’d thy suit.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Shylock thy master spoke with me this day,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And hath preferr’d thee, if it be preferment

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: To leave a rich Jew’s service to become

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: The follower of so poor a gentleman.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: The old proverb is very well parted between my master Shylock and you,

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: sir: you have “the grace of God”, sir, and he hath “enough”.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Thou speak’st it well. Go, father, with thy son.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Take leave of thy old master, and inquire

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: My lodging out. [_To a Servant._] Give him a livery

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: More guarded than his fellows’; see it done.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: Father, in. I cannot get a service, no! I have ne’er a tongue in my

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: head! [_Looking on his palm._] Well, if any man in Italy have a fairer

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: table which doth offer to swear upon a book, I shall have good fortune;

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: go to, here’s a simple line of life. Here’s a small trifle of wives,

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: alas, fifteen wives is nothing; eleven widows and nine maids is a

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: simple coming-in for one man. And then to scape drowning thrice, and to

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: be in peril of my life with the edge of a feather-bed; here are simple

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: ’scapes. Well, if Fortune be a woman, she’s a good wench for this gear.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: Father, come; I’ll take my leave of the Jew in the twinkling.
[_Exeunt Launcelet and Old Gobbo._]

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I pray thee, good Leonardo, think on this.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: These things being bought and orderly bestow’d,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Return in haste, for I do feast tonight

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: My best esteem’d acquaintance; hie thee, go.

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: My best endeavours shall be done herein.
Enter Gratiano.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Where’s your master?

lines.speaker: LEONARDO
lines.text: Yonder, sir, he walks.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Signior Bassanio!

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Gratiano!

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: I have suit to you.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: You have obtain’d it.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: You must not deny me, I must go with you to Belmont.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Why, then you must. But hear thee, Gratiano,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Thou art too wild, too rude, and bold of voice,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Parts that become thee happily enough,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And in such eyes as ours appear not faults;

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: But where thou art not known, why there they show

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Something too liberal. Pray thee, take pain

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: To allay with some cold drops of modesty

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Thy skipping spirit, lest through thy wild behaviour

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I be misconst’red in the place I go to,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And lose my hopes.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Signior Bassanio, hear me.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: If I do not put on a sober habit,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Talk with respect, and swear but now and then,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Wear prayer-books in my pocket, look demurely,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Nay more, while grace is saying, hood mine eyes

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Thus with my hat, and sigh, and say “amen”;

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Use all the observance of civility

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Like one well studied in a sad ostent

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: To please his grandam, never trust me more.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Well, we shall see your bearing.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Nay, but I bar tonight, you shall not gauge me

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: By what we do tonight.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: No, that were pity.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I would entreat you rather to put on

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Your boldest suit of mirth, for we have friends

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: That purpose merriment. But fare you well,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I have some business.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: And I must to Lorenzo and the rest,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: But we will visit you at supper-time.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The same. A room in Shylock’s house.

lines.text: Enter Jessica and Launcelet.

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: I am sorry thou wilt leave my father so.

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: Our house is hell, and thou, a merry devil,

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: Didst rob it of some taste of tediousness.

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: But fare thee well, there is a ducat for thee,

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: And, Launcelet, soon at supper shalt thou see

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: Lorenzo, who is thy new master’s guest.

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: Give him this letter, do it secretly.

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: And so farewell. I would not have my father

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: See me in talk with thee.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: Adieu! tears exhibit my tongue, most beautiful pagan, most sweet Jew!

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: If a Christian do not play the knave and get thee, I am much deceived.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: But, adieu! These foolish drops do something drown my manly spirit.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: Adieu!

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: Farewell, good Launcelet.
[_Exit Launcelet._]

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: Alack, what heinous sin is it in me

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: To be ashamed to be my father’s child!

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: But though I am a daughter to his blood,

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: I am not to his manners. O Lorenzo,

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: If thou keep promise, I shall end this strife,

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: Become a Christian and thy loving wife.
[_Exit._]
Enter Gratiano, Lorenzo, Salarino and Solanio.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Nay, we will slink away in supper-time,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Disguise us at my lodging, and return

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: All in an hour.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: We have not made good preparation.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: We have not spoke us yet of torch-bearers.

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: ’Tis vile, unless it may be quaintly order’d,

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: And better in my mind not undertook.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: ’Tis now but four o’clock, we have two hours

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: To furnish us.
Enter Launcelet with a letter.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Friend Launcelet, what’s the news?

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: And it shall please you to break up this, it shall seem to signify.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: I know the hand, in faith ’tis a fair hand,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: And whiter than the paper it writ on

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Is the fair hand that writ.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Love news, in faith.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: By your leave, sir.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Whither goest thou?

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: Marry, sir, to bid my old master the Jew to sup tonight with my new

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: master the Christian.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Hold here, take this. Tell gentle Jessica

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: I will not fail her, speak it privately.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Go, gentlemen,
[_Exit Launcelet._]

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Will you prepare you for this masque tonight?

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: I am provided of a torch-bearer.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Ay, marry, I’ll be gone about it straight.

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: And so will I.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Meet me and Gratiano

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: At Gratiano’s lodging some hour hence.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: ’Tis good we do so.
[_Exeunt Salarino and Solanio._]

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Was not that letter from fair Jessica?

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: I must needs tell thee all. She hath directed

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: How I shall take her from her father’s house,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: What gold and jewels she is furnish’d with,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: What page’s suit she hath in readiness.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: If e’er the Jew her father come to heaven,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: It will be for his gentle daughter’s sake;

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: And never dare misfortune cross her foot,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Unless she do it under this excuse,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: That she is issue to a faithless Jew.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Come, go with me, peruse this as thou goest;

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Fair Jessica shall be my torch-bearer.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Shylock the Jew and Launcelet his man that was the clown.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Well, thou shalt see, thy eyes shall be thy judge,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: The difference of old Shylock and Bassanio.—

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: What, Jessica!—Thou shalt not gormandize

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: As thou hast done with me;—What, Jessica!—

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: And sleep, and snore, and rend apparel out.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Why, Jessica, I say!

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: Why, Jessica!

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Who bids thee call? I do not bid thee call.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: Your worship was wont to tell me I could do nothing without bidding.
Enter Jessica.

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: Call you? What is your will?

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: I am bid forth to supper, Jessica.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: There are my keys. But wherefore should I go?

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: I am not bid for love, they flatter me.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: But yet I’ll go in hate, to feed upon

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: The prodigal Christian. Jessica, my girl,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Look to my house. I am right loath to go;

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: There is some ill a-brewing towards my rest,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: For I did dream of money-bags tonight.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: I beseech you, sir, go. My young master doth expect your reproach.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: So do I his.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: And they have conspired together. I will not say you shall see a

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: masque, but if you do, then it was not for nothing that my nose fell

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: a-bleeding on Black Monday last at six o’clock i’ th’ morning, falling

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: out that year on Ash-Wednesday was four year in th’ afternoon.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: What, are there masques? Hear you me, Jessica,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Lock up my doors, and when you hear the drum

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: And the vile squealing of the wry-neck’d fife,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Clamber not you up to the casements then,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Nor thrust your head into the public street

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: To gaze on Christian fools with varnish’d faces,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: But stop my house’s ears, I mean my casements.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Let not the sound of shallow fopp’ry enter

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: My sober house. By Jacob’s staff I swear

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: I have no mind of feasting forth tonight.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: But I will go. Go you before me, sirrah.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Say I will come.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: I will go before, sir.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: Mistress, look out at window for all this.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: There will come a Christian by

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: Will be worth a Jewess’ eye.
[_Exit Launcelet._]

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: What says that fool of Hagar’s offspring, ha?

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: His words were “Farewell, mistress,” nothing else.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: The patch is kind enough, but a huge feeder,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Snail-slow in profit, and he sleeps by day

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: More than the wild-cat. Drones hive not with me,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Therefore I part with him, and part with him

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: To one that I would have him help to waste

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: His borrowed purse. Well, Jessica, go in.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Perhaps I will return immediately:

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Do as I bid you, shut doors after you,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: “Fast bind, fast find.”

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: A proverb never stale in thrifty mind.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: Farewell, and if my fortune be not crost,

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: I have a father, you a daughter, lost.
[_Exit._]
Enter the masquers, Gratiano and Salarino.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: This is the penthouse under which Lorenzo

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Desired us to make stand.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: His hour is almost past.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: And it is marvel he out-dwells his hour,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: For lovers ever run before the clock.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: O ten times faster Venus’ pigeons fly

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: To seal love’s bonds new-made than they are wont

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: To keep obliged faith unforfeited!

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: That ever holds: who riseth from a feast

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: With that keen appetite that he sits down?

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Where is the horse that doth untread again

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: His tedious measures with the unbated fire

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: That he did pace them first? All things that are,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Are with more spirit chased than enjoy’d.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: How like a younger or a prodigal

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: The scarfed bark puts from her native bay,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Hugg’d and embraced by the strumpet wind!

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: How like the prodigal doth she return

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: With over-weather’d ribs and ragged sails,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Lean, rent, and beggar’d by the strumpet wind!
Enter Lorenzo.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Here comes Lorenzo, more of this hereafter.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Sweet friends, your patience for my long abode.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Not I but my affairs have made you wait.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: When you shall please to play the thieves for wives,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: I’ll watch as long for you then. Approach.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Here dwells my father Jew. Ho! who’s within?
Enter Jessica above, in boy’s clothes.

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: Who are you? Tell me, for more certainty,

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: Albeit I’ll swear that I do know your tongue.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Lorenzo, and thy love.

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: Lorenzo certain, and my love indeed,

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: For who love I so much? And now who knows

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: But you, Lorenzo, whether I am yours?

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Heaven and thy thoughts are witness that thou art.

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: Here, catch this casket; it is worth the pains.

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: I am glad ’tis night, you do not look on me,

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: For I am much asham’d of my exchange.

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: But love is blind, and lovers cannot see

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: The pretty follies that themselves commit,

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: For if they could, Cupid himself would blush

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: To see me thus transformed to a boy.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Descend, for you must be my torch-bearer.

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: What! must I hold a candle to my shames?

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: They in themselves, good sooth, are too too light.

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: Why, ’tis an office of discovery, love,

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: And I should be obscur’d.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: So are you, sweet,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Even in the lovely garnish of a boy.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: But come at once,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: For the close night doth play the runaway,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: And we are stay’d for at Bassanio’s feast.

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: I will make fast the doors, and gild myself

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: With some moe ducats, and be with you straight.
[_Exit above._]

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Now, by my hood, a gentle, and no Jew.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Beshrew me but I love her heartily,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: For she is wise, if I can judge of her,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: And fair she is, if that mine eyes be true,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: And true she is, as she hath prov’d herself.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: And therefore, like herself, wise, fair, and true,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Shall she be placed in my constant soul.
Enter Jessica.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: What, art thou come? On, gentlemen, away!

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Our masquing mates by this time for us stay.
[_Exit with Jessica and Salarino._]
Enter Antonio.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Who’s there?

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Signior Antonio!

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Fie, fie, Gratiano! where are all the rest?

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: ’Tis nine o’clock, our friends all stay for you.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: No masque tonight, the wind is come about;

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Bassanio presently will go aboard.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I have sent twenty out to seek for you.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: I am glad on’t. I desire no more delight

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Than to be under sail and gone tonight.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Belmont. A room in Portia’s house.

lines.text: Flourish of cornets. Enter Portia with the Prince of Morocco and both their trains.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Go, draw aside the curtains and discover

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: The several caskets to this noble prince.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Now make your choice.

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: The first, of gold, who this inscription bears,

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: “Who chooseth me shall gain what many men desire.”

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: The second, silver, which this promise carries,

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: “Who chooseth me shall get as much as he deserves.”

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: This third, dull lead, with warning all as blunt,

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: “Who chooseth me must give and hazard all he hath.”

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: How shall I know if I do choose the right?

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: The one of them contains my picture, prince.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: If you choose that, then I am yours withal.

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Some god direct my judgment! Let me see.

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: I will survey the inscriptions back again.

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: What says this leaden casket?

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: “Who chooseth me must give and hazard all he hath.”

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Must give, for what? For lead? Hazard for lead!

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: This casket threatens; men that hazard all

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Do it in hope of fair advantages:

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: A golden mind stoops not to shows of dross,

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: I’ll then nor give nor hazard aught for lead.

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: What says the silver with her virgin hue?

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: “Who chooseth me shall get as much as he deserves.”

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: As much as he deserves! Pause there, Morocco,

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: And weigh thy value with an even hand.

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: If thou be’st rated by thy estimation

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Thou dost deserve enough, and yet enough

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: May not extend so far as to the lady.

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: And yet to be afeard of my deserving

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Were but a weak disabling of myself.

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: As much as I deserve! Why, that’s the lady:

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: I do in birth deserve her, and in fortunes,

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: In graces, and in qualities of breeding;

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: But more than these, in love I do deserve.

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: What if I stray’d no farther, but chose here?

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Let’s see once more this saying grav’d in gold:

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: “Who chooseth me shall gain what many men desire.”

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Why, that’s the lady, all the world desires her.

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: From the four corners of the earth they come

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: To kiss this shrine, this mortal breathing saint.

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: The Hyrcanian deserts and the vasty wilds

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Of wide Arabia are as throughfares now

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: For princes to come view fair Portia.

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: The watery kingdom, whose ambitious head

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Spets in the face of heaven, is no bar

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: To stop the foreign spirits, but they come

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: As o’er a brook to see fair Portia.

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: One of these three contains her heavenly picture.

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Is’t like that lead contains her? ’Twere damnation

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: To think so base a thought. It were too gross

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: To rib her cerecloth in the obscure grave.

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Or shall I think in silver she’s immur’d

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Being ten times undervalued to tried gold?

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: O sinful thought! Never so rich a gem

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Was set in worse than gold. They have in England

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: A coin that bears the figure of an angel

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Stamped in gold; but that’s insculp’d upon;

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: But here an angel in a golden bed

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Lies all within. Deliver me the key.

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Here do I choose, and thrive I as I may.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: There, take it, prince, and if my form lie there,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Then I am yours.
[_He unlocks the golden casket._]

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: O hell! what have we here?

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: A carrion Death, within whose empty eye

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: There is a written scroll. I’ll read the writing.

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: _All that glisters is not gold,

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Often have you heard that told.

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Many a man his life hath sold

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: But my outside to behold.

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Gilded tombs do worms infold.

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Had you been as wise as bold,

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Young in limbs, in judgment old,

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Your answer had not been inscroll’d,

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Fare you well, your suit is cold._

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Cold indeed and labour lost,

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Then farewell heat, and welcome frost.

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: Portia, adieu! I have too griev’d a heart

lines.speaker: PRINCE OF MOROCCO
lines.text: To take a tedious leave. Thus losers part.
[_Exit with his train. Flourish of cornets._]

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: A gentle riddance. Draw the curtains, go.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Let all of his complexion choose me so.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Salarino and Solanio.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Why, man, I saw Bassanio under sail;

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: With him is Gratiano gone along;

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: And in their ship I am sure Lorenzo is not.

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: The villain Jew with outcries rais’d the Duke,

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: Who went with him to search Bassanio’s ship.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: He came too late, the ship was under sail;

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: But there the Duke was given to understand

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: That in a gondola were seen together

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Lorenzo and his amorous Jessica.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Besides, Antonio certified the Duke

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: They were not with Bassanio in his ship.

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: I never heard a passion so confus’d,

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: So strange, outrageous, and so variable

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: As the dog Jew did utter in the streets.

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: “My daughter! O my ducats! O my daughter!

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: Fled with a Christian! O my Christian ducats!

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: Justice! the law! my ducats and my daughter!

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: A sealed bag, two sealed bags of ducats,

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: Of double ducats, stol’n from me by my daughter!

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: And jewels, two stones, two rich and precious stones,

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: Stol’n by my daughter! Justice! find the girl,

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: She hath the stones upon her and the ducats.”

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Why, all the boys in Venice follow him,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Crying, his stones, his daughter, and his ducats.

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: Let good Antonio look he keep his day

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: Or he shall pay for this.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Marry, well rememb’red.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: I reason’d with a Frenchman yesterday,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Who told me, in the narrow seas that part

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: The French and English, there miscarried

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: A vessel of our country richly fraught.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: I thought upon Antonio when he told me,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: And wish’d in silence that it were not his.

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: You were best to tell Antonio what you hear,

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: Yet do not suddenly, for it may grieve him.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: A kinder gentleman treads not the earth.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: I saw Bassanio and Antonio part,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Bassanio told him he would make some speed

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Of his return. He answered “Do not so,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Slubber not business for my sake, Bassanio,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: But stay the very riping of the time,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: And for the Jew’s bond which he hath of me,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Let it not enter in your mind of love:

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Be merry, and employ your chiefest thoughts

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: To courtship, and such fair ostents of love

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: As shall conveniently become you there.”

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: And even there, his eye being big with tears,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Turning his face, he put his hand behind him,

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: And with affection wondrous sensible

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: He wrung Bassanio’s hand, and so they parted.

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: I think he only loves the world for him.

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: I pray thee, let us go and find him out

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: And quicken his embraced heaviness

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: With some delight or other.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Do we so.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Belmont. A room in Portia’s house.

lines.text: Enter Nerissa and a Servitor.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: Quick, quick, I pray thee, draw the curtain straight.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: The Prince of Arragon hath ta’en his oath,

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: And comes to his election presently.
Flourish of cornets. Enter the Prince of Arragon, his train, and Portia.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Behold, there stand the caskets, noble Prince,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: If you choose that wherein I am contain’d,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Straight shall our nuptial rites be solemniz’d.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: But if you fail, without more speech, my lord,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: You must be gone from hence immediately.

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: I am enjoin’d by oath to observe three things:

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: First, never to unfold to anyone

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Which casket ’twas I chose; next, if I fail

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Of the right casket, never in my life

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: To woo a maid in way of marriage;

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Lastly,

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: If I do fail in fortune of my choice,

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Immediately to leave you and be gone.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: To these injunctions everyone doth swear

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: That comes to hazard for my worthless self.

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: And so have I address’d me. Fortune now

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: To my heart’s hope! Gold, silver, and base lead.

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: “Who chooseth me must give and hazard all he hath.”

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: You shall look fairer ere I give or hazard.

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: What says the golden chest? Ha! let me see:

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: “Who chooseth me shall gain what many men desire.”

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: What many men desire! that “many” may be meant

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: By the fool multitude, that choose by show,

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Not learning more than the fond eye doth teach,

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Which pries not to th’ interior, but like the martlet

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Builds in the weather on the outward wall,

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Even in the force and road of casualty.

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: I will not choose what many men desire,

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Because I will not jump with common spirits

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: And rank me with the barbarous multitudes.

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Why, then to thee, thou silver treasure-house,

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Tell me once more what title thou dost bear.

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: “Who chooseth me shall get as much as he deserves.”

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: And well said too; for who shall go about

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: To cozen fortune, and be honourable

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Without the stamp of merit? Let none presume

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: To wear an undeserved dignity.

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: O that estates, degrees, and offices

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Were not deriv’d corruptly, and that clear honour

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Were purchas’d by the merit of the wearer!

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: How many then should cover that stand bare?

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: How many be commanded that command?

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: How much low peasantry would then be gleaned

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: From the true seed of honour? And how much honour

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Pick’d from the chaff and ruin of the times,

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: To be new varnish’d? Well, but to my choice.

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: “Who chooseth me shall get as much as he deserves.”

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: I will assume desert. Give me a key for this,

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: And instantly unlock my fortunes here.
[_He opens the silver casket._]

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Too long a pause for that which you find there.

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: What’s here? The portrait of a blinking idiot

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Presenting me a schedule! I will read it.

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: How much unlike art thou to Portia!

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: How much unlike my hopes and my deservings!

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: “Who chooseth me shall have as much as he deserves.”

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Did I deserve no more than a fool’s head?

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Is that my prize? Are my deserts no better?

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: To offend and judge are distinct offices,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And of opposed natures.

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: What is here?

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: _The fire seven times tried this;

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Seven times tried that judgment is

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: That did never choose amiss.

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Some there be that shadows kiss;

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Such have but a shadow’s bliss.

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: There be fools alive, I wis,

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Silver’d o’er, and so was this.

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Take what wife you will to bed,

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: I will ever be your head:

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: So be gone; you are sped._

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Still more fool I shall appear

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: By the time I linger here.

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: With one fool’s head I came to woo,

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: But I go away with two.

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Sweet, adieu! I’ll keep my oath,

lines.speaker: ARRAGON
lines.text: Patiently to bear my wroth.
[_Exit Arragon with his train._]

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Thus hath the candle sing’d the moth.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: O, these deliberate fools! When they do choose,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: They have the wisdom by their wit to lose.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: The ancient saying is no heresy:

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: Hanging and wiving goes by destiny.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Come, draw the curtain, Nerissa.
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Where is my lady?

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Here. What would my lord?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Madam, there is alighted at your gate

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: A young Venetian, one that comes before

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: To signify th’ approaching of his lord,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: From whom he bringeth sensible regreets;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: To wit (besides commends and courteous breath)

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Gifts of rich value; yet I have not seen

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: So likely an ambassador of love.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: A day in April never came so sweet,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: To show how costly summer was at hand,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: As this fore-spurrer comes before his lord.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: No more, I pray thee. I am half afeard

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Thou wilt say anon he is some kin to thee,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Thou spend’st such high-day wit in praising him.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Come, come, Nerissa, for I long to see

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Quick Cupid’s post that comes so mannerly.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: Bassanio, Lord Love, if thy will it be!
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Solanio and Salarino.

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: Now, what news on the Rialto?

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Why, yet it lives there unchecked that Antonio hath a ship of rich

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: lading wrack’d on the narrow seas; the Goodwins, I think they call the

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: place, a very dangerous flat and fatal, where the carcasses of many a

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: tall ship lie buried, as they say, if my gossip Report be an honest

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: woman of her word.

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: I would she were as lying a gossip in that as ever knapped ginger or

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: made her neighbours believe she wept for the death of a third husband.

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: But it is true, without any slips of prolixity or crossing the plain

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: highway of talk, that the good Antonio, the honest Antonio,—O that I

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: had a title good enough to keep his name company!—

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Come, the full stop.

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: Ha, what sayest thou? Why, the end is, he hath lost a ship.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: I would it might prove the end of his losses.

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: Let me say “amen” betimes, lest the devil cross my prayer, for here he

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: comes in the likeness of a Jew.
Enter Shylock.

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: How now, Shylock, what news among the merchants?

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: You knew, none so well, none so well as you, of my daughter’s flight.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: That’s certain, I, for my part, knew the tailor that made the wings she

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: flew withal.

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: And Shylock, for his own part, knew the bird was fledged; and then it

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: is the complexion of them all to leave the dam.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: She is damn’d for it.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: That’s certain, if the devil may be her judge.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: My own flesh and blood to rebel!

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: Out upon it, old carrion! Rebels it at these years?

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: I say my daughter is my flesh and my blood.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: There is more difference between thy flesh and hers than between jet

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: and ivory, more between your bloods than there is between red wine and

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Rhenish. But tell us, do you hear whether Antonio have had any loss at

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: sea or no?

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: There I have another bad match, a bankrupt, a prodigal, who dare scarce

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: show his head on the Rialto, a beggar that used to come so smug upon

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: the mart; let him look to his bond. He was wont to call me usurer; let

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: him look to his bond: he was wont to lend money for a Christian cur’sy;

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: let him look to his bond.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Why, I am sure if he forfeit, thou wilt not take his flesh! What’s that

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: good for?

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: To bait fish withal; if it will feed nothing else, it will feed my

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
