lines.text: revenge. He hath disgrac’d me and hind’red me half a million, laugh’d

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: at my losses, mock’d at my gains, scorned my nation, thwarted my

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: bargains, cooled my friends, heated mine enemies. And what’s his

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: reason? I am a Jew. Hath not a Jew eyes? Hath not a Jew hands, organs,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: dimensions, senses, affections, passions? Fed with the same food, hurt

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: with the same weapons, subject to the same diseases, healed by the same

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: means, warmed and cooled by the same winter and summer as a Christian

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: is? If you prick us, do we not bleed? If you tickle us, do we not

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: laugh? If you poison us, do we not die? And if you wrong us, shall we

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: not revenge? If we are like you in the rest, we will resemble you in

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: that. If a Jew wrong a Christian, what is his humility? Revenge. If a

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Christian wrong a Jew, what should his sufferance be by Christian

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: example? Why, revenge! The villainy you teach me I will execute, and it

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: shall go hard but I will better the instruction.
Enter a man from Antonio.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Gentlemen, my master Antonio is at his house, and desires to speak with

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: you both.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: We have been up and down to seek him.
Enter Tubal.

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: Here comes another of the tribe; a third cannot be match’d, unless the

lines.speaker: SOLANIO
lines.text: devil himself turn Jew.
[_Exeunt Solanio, Salarino and the Servant._]

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: How now, Tubal, what news from Genoa? Hast thou found my daughter?

lines.speaker: TUBAL
lines.text: I often came where I did hear of her, but cannot find her.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Why there, there, there, there! A diamond gone cost me two thousand

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: ducats in Frankfort! The curse never fell upon our nation till now, I

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: never felt it till now. Two thousand ducats in that, and other

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: precious, precious jewels. I would my daughter were dead at my foot,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: and the jewels in her ear; would she were hearsed at my foot, and the

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: ducats in her coffin. No news of them? Why so? And I know not what’s

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: spent in the search. Why, thou—loss upon loss! The thief gone with so

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: much, and so much to find the thief, and no satisfaction, no revenge,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: nor no ill luck stirring but what lights o’ my shoulders, no sighs but

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: o’ my breathing, no tears but o’ my shedding.

lines.speaker: TUBAL
lines.text: Yes, other men have ill luck too. Antonio, as I heard in Genoa—

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: What, what, what? Ill luck, ill luck?

lines.speaker: TUBAL
lines.text: —hath an argosy cast away coming from Tripolis.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: I thank God! I thank God! Is it true, is it true?

lines.speaker: TUBAL
lines.text: I spoke with some of the sailors that escaped the wrack.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: I thank thee, good Tubal. Good news, good news! Ha, ha, heard in Genoa?

lines.speaker: TUBAL
lines.text: Your daughter spent in Genoa, as I heard, one night, fourscore ducats.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Thou stick’st a dagger in me. I shall never see my gold again.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Fourscore ducats at a sitting! Fourscore ducats!

lines.speaker: TUBAL
lines.text: There came divers of Antonio’s creditors in my company to Venice that

lines.speaker: TUBAL
lines.text: swear he cannot choose but break.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: I am very glad of it. I’ll plague him, I’ll torture him. I am glad of

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: it.

lines.speaker: TUBAL
lines.text: One of them showed me a ring that he had of your daughter for a monkey.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Out upon her! Thou torturest me, Tubal. It was my turquoise, I had it

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: of Leah when I was a bachelor. I would not have given it for a

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: wilderness of monkeys.

lines.speaker: TUBAL
lines.text: But Antonio is certainly undone.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Nay, that’s true, that’s very true. Go, Tubal, fee me an officer;

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: bespeak him a fortnight before. I will have the heart of him if he

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: forfeit, for were he out of Venice I can make what merchandise I will.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Go, Tubal, and meet me at our synagogue. Go, good Tubal, at our

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: synagogue, Tubal.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Belmont. A room in Portia’s house.

lines.text: Enter Bassanio, Portia, Gratiano, Nerissa and all their trains.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I pray you tarry, pause a day or two

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Before you hazard, for in choosing wrong

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I lose your company; therefore forbear a while.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: There’s something tells me (but it is not love)

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I would not lose you, and you know yourself

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Hate counsels not in such a quality.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: But lest you should not understand me well,—

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And yet a maiden hath no tongue but thought,—

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I would detain you here some month or two

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Before you venture for me. I could teach you

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: How to choose right, but then I am forsworn.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: So will I never be. So may you miss me.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: But if you do, you’ll make me wish a sin,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: That I had been forsworn. Beshrew your eyes,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: They have o’erlook’d me and divided me.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: One half of me is yours, the other half yours,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Mine own, I would say; but if mine, then yours,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And so all yours. O these naughty times

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Puts bars between the owners and their rights!

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And so though yours, not yours. Prove it so,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Let Fortune go to hell for it, not I.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I speak too long, but ’tis to peise the time,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: To eche it, and to draw it out in length,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: To stay you from election.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Let me choose,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: For as I am, I live upon the rack.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Upon the rack, Bassanio! Then confess

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: What treason there is mingled with your love.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: None but that ugly treason of mistrust,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Which makes me fear th’ enjoying of my love.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: There may as well be amity and life

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: ’Tween snow and fire as treason and my love.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Ay, but I fear you speak upon the rack

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Where men enforced do speak anything.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Promise me life, and I’ll confess the truth.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Well then, confess and live.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: “Confess and love”

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Had been the very sum of my confession:

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: O happy torment, when my torturer

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Doth teach me answers for deliverance!

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: But let me to my fortune and the caskets.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Away, then! I am lock’d in one of them.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: If you do love me, you will find me out.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Nerissa and the rest, stand all aloof.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Let music sound while he doth make his choice.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Then if he lose he makes a swan-like end,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Fading in music. That the comparison

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: May stand more proper, my eye shall be the stream

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And wat’ry death-bed for him. He may win,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And what is music then? Then music is

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Even as the flourish when true subjects bow

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: To a new-crowned monarch. Such it is

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: As are those dulcet sounds in break of day

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: That creep into the dreaming bridegroom’s ear

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And summon him to marriage. Now he goes,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: With no less presence, but with much more love

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Than young Alcides when he did redeem

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: The virgin tribute paid by howling Troy

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: To the sea-monster: I stand for sacrifice;

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: The rest aloof are the Dardanian wives,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: With bleared visages come forth to view

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: The issue of th’ exploit. Go, Hercules!

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Live thou, I live. With much much more dismay

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I view the fight than thou that mak’st the fray.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: A song, whilst Bassanio comments on the caskets to himself.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: _Tell me where is fancy bred,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Or in the heart or in the head?

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: How begot, how nourished?

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Reply, reply.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: It is engend’red in the eyes,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: With gazing fed, and fancy dies

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: In the cradle where it lies.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Let us all ring fancy’s knell:

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I’ll begin it.—Ding, dong, bell._

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: _Ding, dong, bell._

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: So may the outward shows be least themselves.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: The world is still deceiv’d with ornament.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: In law, what plea so tainted and corrupt

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: But, being season’d with a gracious voice,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Obscures the show of evil? In religion,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: What damned error but some sober brow

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Will bless it, and approve it with a text,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Hiding the grossness with fair ornament?

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: There is no vice so simple but assumes

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Some mark of virtue on his outward parts.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: How many cowards, whose hearts are all as false

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: As stairs of sand, wear yet upon their chins

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: The beards of Hercules and frowning Mars,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Who inward search’d, have livers white as milk,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And these assume but valour’s excrement

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: To render them redoubted. Look on beauty,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And you shall see ’tis purchas’d by the weight,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Which therein works a miracle in nature,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Making them lightest that wear most of it:

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: So are those crisped snaky golden locks

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Which make such wanton gambols with the wind

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Upon supposed fairness, often known

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: To be the dowry of a second head,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: The skull that bred them in the sepulchre.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Thus ornament is but the guiled shore

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: To a most dangerous sea; the beauteous scarf

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Veiling an Indian beauty; in a word,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: The seeming truth which cunning times put on

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: To entrap the wisest. Therefore thou gaudy gold,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Hard food for Midas, I will none of thee,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Nor none of thee, thou pale and common drudge

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: ’Tween man and man: but thou, thou meagre lead,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Which rather threaten’st than dost promise aught,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Thy palenness moves me more than eloquence,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And here choose I, joy be the consequence!
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: How all the other passions fleet to air,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: As doubtful thoughts, and rash-embrac’d despair,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And shudd’ring fear, and green-ey’d jealousy.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: O love, be moderate; allay thy ecstasy,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: In measure rain thy joy; scant this excess!

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I feel too much thy blessing, make it less,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: For fear I surfeit.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: What find I here?
[_Opening the leaden casket_.]

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Fair Portia’s counterfeit! What demi-god

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Hath come so near creation? Move these eyes?

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Or whether, riding on the balls of mine,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Seem they in motion? Here are sever’d lips,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Parted with sugar breath, so sweet a bar

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Should sunder such sweet friends. Here in her hairs

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: The painter plays the spider, and hath woven

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: A golden mesh t’entrap the hearts of men

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Faster than gnats in cobwebs. But her eyes!—

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: How could he see to do them? Having made one,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Methinks it should have power to steal both his

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And leave itself unfurnish’d. Yet look how far

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: The substance of my praise doth wrong this shadow

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: In underprizing it, so far this shadow

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Doth limp behind the substance. Here’s the scroll,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: The continent and summary of my fortune.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: _You that choose not by the view

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Chance as fair and choose as true!

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Since this fortune falls to you,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Be content and seek no new.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: If you be well pleas’d with this,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And hold your fortune for your bliss,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Turn to where your lady is,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And claim her with a loving kiss._

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: A gentle scroll. Fair lady, by your leave,
[_Kissing her_.]

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I come by note to give and to receive.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Like one of two contending in a prize

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: That thinks he hath done well in people’s eyes,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Hearing applause and universal shout,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Giddy in spirit, still gazing in a doubt

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Whether those peals of praise be his or no,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: So, thrice-fair lady, stand I even so,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: As doubtful whether what I see be true,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Until confirm’d, sign’d, ratified by you.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: You see me, Lord Bassanio, where I stand,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Such as I am; though for myself alone

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I would not be ambitious in my wish

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: To wish myself much better, yet for you

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I would be trebled twenty times myself,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: A thousand times more fair, ten thousand times

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: More rich,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: That only to stand high in your account,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I might in virtues, beauties, livings, friends,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Exceed account. But the full sum of me

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Is sum of something, which, to term in gross,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Is an unlesson’d girl, unschool’d, unpractis’d;

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Happy in this, she is not yet so old

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: But she may learn; happier than this,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: She is not bred so dull but she can learn;

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Happiest of all, is that her gentle spirit

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Commits itself to yours to be directed,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: As from her lord, her governor, her king.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Myself, and what is mine, to you and yours

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Is now converted. But now I was the lord

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Of this fair mansion, master of my servants,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Queen o’er myself; and even now, but now,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: This house, these servants, and this same myself

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Are yours,—my lord’s. I give them with this ring,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Which when you part from, lose, or give away,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Let it presage the ruin of your love,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And be my vantage to exclaim on you.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Madam, you have bereft me of all words,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Only my blood speaks to you in my veins,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And there is such confusion in my powers

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: As after some oration fairly spoke

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: By a beloved prince, there doth appear

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Among the buzzing pleased multitude,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Where every something being blent together,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Turns to a wild of nothing, save of joy

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Express’d and not express’d. But when this ring

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Parts from this finger, then parts life from hence.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: O then be bold to say Bassanio’s dead!

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: My lord and lady, it is now our time,

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: That have stood by and seen our wishes prosper,

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: To cry, good joy. Good joy, my lord and lady!

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: My Lord Bassanio, and my gentle lady,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: I wish you all the joy that you can wish;

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: For I am sure you can wish none from me.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: And when your honours mean to solemnize

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: The bargain of your faith, I do beseech you

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Even at that time I may be married too.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: With all my heart, so thou canst get a wife.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: I thank your lordship, you have got me one.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: My eyes, my lord, can look as swift as yours:

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: You saw the mistress, I beheld the maid.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: You lov’d, I lov’d; for intermission

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: No more pertains to me, my lord, than you.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Your fortune stood upon the caskets there,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: And so did mine too, as the matter falls.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: For wooing here until I sweat again,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: And swearing till my very roof was dry

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: With oaths of love, at last, (if promise last)

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: I got a promise of this fair one here

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: To have her love, provided that your fortune

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Achiev’d her mistress.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Is this true, Nerissa?

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: Madam, it is, so you stand pleas’d withal.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And do you, Gratiano, mean good faith?

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Yes, faith, my lord.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Our feast shall be much honoured in your marriage.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: We’ll play with them the first boy for a thousand ducats.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: What! and stake down?

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: No, we shall ne’er win at that sport and stake down.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: But who comes here? Lorenzo and his infidel?

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: What, and my old Venetian friend, Salerio!
Enter Lorenzo, Jessica and Salerio.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Lorenzo and Salerio, welcome hither,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: If that the youth of my new int’rest here

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Have power to bid you welcome. By your leave,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I bid my very friends and countrymen,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Sweet Portia, welcome.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: So do I, my lord,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: They are entirely welcome.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: I thank your honour. For my part, my lord,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: My purpose was not to have seen you here,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: But meeting with Salerio by the way,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: He did entreat me, past all saying nay,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: To come with him along.

lines.speaker: SALERIO
lines.text: I did, my lord,

lines.speaker: SALERIO
lines.text: And I have reason for it. Signior Antonio

lines.speaker: SALERIO
lines.text: Commends him to you.
[_Gives Bassanio a letter._]

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Ere I ope his letter,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I pray you tell me how my good friend doth.

lines.speaker: SALERIO
lines.text: Not sick, my lord, unless it be in mind,

lines.speaker: SALERIO
lines.text: Nor well, unless in mind. His letter there

lines.speaker: SALERIO
lines.text: Will show you his estate.
[_Bassanio opens the letter._]

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Nerissa, cheer yond stranger, bid her welcome.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Your hand, Salerio. What’s the news from Venice?

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: How doth that royal merchant, good Antonio?

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: I know he will be glad of our success.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: We are the Jasons, we have won the fleece.

lines.speaker: SALERIO
lines.text: I would you had won the fleece that he hath lost.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: There are some shrewd contents in yond same paper

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: That steals the colour from Bassanio’s cheek.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Some dear friend dead, else nothing in the world

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Could turn so much the constitution

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Of any constant man. What, worse and worse?

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: With leave, Bassanio, I am half yourself,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And I must freely have the half of anything

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: That this same paper brings you.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: O sweet Portia,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Here are a few of the unpleasant’st words

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: That ever blotted paper. Gentle lady,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: When I did first impart my love to you,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I freely told you all the wealth I had

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Ran in my veins, I was a gentleman.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And then I told you true. And yet, dear lady,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Rating myself at nothing, you shall see

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: How much I was a braggart. When I told you

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: My state was nothing, I should then have told you

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: That I was worse than nothing; for indeed

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I have engag’d myself to a dear friend,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Engag’d my friend to his mere enemy,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: To feed my means. Here is a letter, lady,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: The paper as the body of my friend,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And every word in it a gaping wound

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Issuing life-blood. But is it true, Salerio?

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Hath all his ventures fail’d? What, not one hit?

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: From Tripolis, from Mexico, and England,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: From Lisbon, Barbary, and India,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And not one vessel scape the dreadful touch

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Of merchant-marring rocks?

lines.speaker: SALERIO
lines.text: Not one, my lord.

lines.speaker: SALERIO
lines.text: Besides, it should appear, that if he had

lines.speaker: SALERIO
lines.text: The present money to discharge the Jew,

lines.speaker: SALERIO
lines.text: He would not take it. Never did I know

lines.speaker: SALERIO
lines.text: A creature that did bear the shape of man

lines.speaker: SALERIO
lines.text: So keen and greedy to confound a man.

lines.speaker: SALERIO
lines.text: He plies the Duke at morning and at night,

lines.speaker: SALERIO
lines.text: And doth impeach the freedom of the state

lines.speaker: SALERIO
lines.text: If they deny him justice. Twenty merchants,

lines.speaker: SALERIO
lines.text: The Duke himself, and the magnificoes

lines.speaker: SALERIO
lines.text: Of greatest port have all persuaded with him,

lines.speaker: SALERIO
lines.text: But none can drive him from the envious plea

lines.speaker: SALERIO
lines.text: Of forfeiture, of justice, and his bond.

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: When I was with him, I have heard him swear

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: To Tubal and to Chus, his countrymen,

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: That he would rather have Antonio’s flesh

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: Than twenty times the value of the sum

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: That he did owe him. And I know, my lord,

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: If law, authority, and power deny not,

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: It will go hard with poor Antonio.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Is it your dear friend that is thus in trouble?

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: The dearest friend to me, the kindest man,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: The best condition’d and unwearied spirit

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: In doing courtesies, and one in whom

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: The ancient Roman honour more appears

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Than any that draws breath in Italy.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: What sum owes he the Jew?

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: For me three thousand ducats.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: What, no more?

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Pay him six thousand, and deface the bond.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Double six thousand, and then treble that,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Before a friend of this description

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Shall lose a hair through Bassanio’s fault.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: First go with me to church and call me wife,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And then away to Venice to your friend.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: For never shall you lie by Portia’s side

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: With an unquiet soul. You shall have gold

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: To pay the petty debt twenty times over.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: When it is paid, bring your true friend along.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: My maid Nerissa and myself meantime,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Will live as maids and widows. Come, away!

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: For you shall hence upon your wedding day.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Bid your friends welcome, show a merry cheer;

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Since you are dear bought, I will love you dear.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: But let me hear the letter of your friend.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: _Sweet Bassanio, my ships have all miscarried, my creditors grow cruel,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: my estate is very low, my bond to the Jew is forfeit, and since in

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: paying it, it is impossible I should live, all debts are clear’d

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: between you and I, if I might but see you at my death. Notwithstanding,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: use your pleasure. If your love do not persuade you to come, let not my

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: letter._

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: O love, dispatch all business and be gone!

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Since I have your good leave to go away,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I will make haste; but, till I come again,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: No bed shall e’er be guilty of my stay,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Nor rest be interposer ’twixt us twain.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Shylock, Salarino, Antonio and Gaoler.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Gaoler, look to him. Tell not me of mercy.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: This is the fool that lent out money gratis.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Gaoler, look to him.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Hear me yet, good Shylock.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: I’ll have my bond, speak not against my bond.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: I have sworn an oath that I will have my bond.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Thou call’dst me dog before thou hadst a cause,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: But since I am a dog, beware my fangs;

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: The Duke shall grant me justice. I do wonder,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: Thou naughty gaoler, that thou art so fond

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: To come abroad with him at his request.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I pray thee hear me speak.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: I’ll have my bond. I will not hear thee speak.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: I’ll have my bond, and therefore speak no more.

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: I’ll not be made a soft and dull-eyed fool,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: To shake the head, relent, and sigh, and yield

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: To Christian intercessors. Follow not,

lines.speaker: SHYLOCK
lines.text: I’ll have no speaking, I will have my bond.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: It is the most impenetrable cur

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: That ever kept with men.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Let him alone.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I’ll follow him no more with bootless prayers.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: He seeks my life, his reason well I know:

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I oft deliver’d from his forfeitures

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Many that have at times made moan to me.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Therefore he hates me.

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: I am sure the Duke

lines.speaker: SALARINO
lines.text: Will never grant this forfeiture to hold.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: The Duke cannot deny the course of law,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: For the commodity that strangers have

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: With us in Venice, if it be denied,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: ’Twill much impeach the justice of the state,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Since that the trade and profit of the city

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Consisteth of all nations. Therefore, go.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: These griefs and losses have so bated me

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: That I shall hardly spare a pound of flesh

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Tomorrow to my bloody creditor.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Well, gaoler, on, pray God Bassanio come

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: To see me pay his debt, and then I care not.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Belmont. A room in Portia’s house.

lines.text: Enter Portia, Nerissa, Lorenzo, Jessica and Balthazar.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Madam, although I speak it in your presence,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: You have a noble and a true conceit

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Of godlike amity, which appears most strongly

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: In bearing thus the absence of your lord.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: But if you knew to whom you show this honour,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: How true a gentleman you send relief,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: How dear a lover of my lord your husband,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: I know you would be prouder of the work

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Than customary bounty can enforce you.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I never did repent for doing good,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Nor shall not now; for in companions

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: That do converse and waste the time together,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Whose souls do bear an equal yoke of love,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: There must be needs a like proportion

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Of lineaments, of manners, and of spirit;

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Which makes me think that this Antonio,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Being the bosom lover of my lord,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Must needs be like my lord. If it be so,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: How little is the cost I have bestowed

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: In purchasing the semblance of my soul

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: From out the state of hellish cruelty!

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: This comes too near the praising of myself;

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Therefore no more of it. Hear other things.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Lorenzo, I commit into your hands

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: The husbandry and manage of my house

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Until my lord’s return. For mine own part,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I have toward heaven breath’d a secret vow

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: To live in prayer and contemplation,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Only attended by Nerissa here,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Until her husband and my lord’s return.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: There is a monastery two miles off,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And there we will abide. I do desire you

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Not to deny this imposition,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: The which my love and some necessity

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Now lays upon you.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Madam, with all my heart

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: I shall obey you in all fair commands.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: My people do already know my mind,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And will acknowledge you and Jessica

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: In place of Lord Bassanio and myself.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: So fare you well till we shall meet again.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Fair thoughts and happy hours attend on you!

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: I wish your ladyship all heart’s content.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I thank you for your wish, and am well pleas’d

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: To wish it back on you. Fare you well, Jessica.
[_Exeunt Jessica and Lorenzo._]

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Now, Balthazar,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: As I have ever found thee honest-true,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: So let me find thee still. Take this same letter,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And use thou all th’ endeavour of a man

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: In speed to Padua, see thou render this

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Into my cousin’s hands, Doctor Bellario;

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And look what notes and garments he doth give thee,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Bring them, I pray thee, with imagin’d speed

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Unto the traject, to the common ferry

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Which trades to Venice. Waste no time in words,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: But get thee gone. I shall be there before thee.

lines.speaker: BALTHAZAR
lines.text: Madam, I go with all convenient speed.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Come on, Nerissa, I have work in hand

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: That you yet know not of; we’ll see our husbands

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Before they think of us.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: Shall they see us?

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: They shall, Nerissa, but in such a habit

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: That they shall think we are accomplished

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: With that we lack. I’ll hold thee any wager,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: When we are both accoutered like young men,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I’ll prove the prettier fellow of the two,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And wear my dagger with the braver grace,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And speak between the change of man and boy

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: With a reed voice; and turn two mincing steps

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Into a manly stride; and speak of frays

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Like a fine bragging youth; and tell quaint lies

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: How honourable ladies sought my love,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Which I denying, they fell sick and died;

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I could not do withal. Then I’ll repent,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And wish for all that, that I had not kill’d them.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And twenty of these puny lies I’ll tell,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: That men shall swear I have discontinued school

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: About a twelvemonth. I have within my mind

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: A thousand raw tricks of these bragging Jacks,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Which I will practise.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: Why, shall we turn to men?

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Fie, what a question’s that,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: If thou wert near a lewd interpreter!

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: But come, I’ll tell thee all my whole device

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: When I am in my coach, which stays for us

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: At the park gate; and therefore haste away,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: For we must measure twenty miles today.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Launcelet and Jessica.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: Yes, truly, for look you, the sins of the father are to be laid upon

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: the children, therefore, I promise you, I fear you. I was always plain

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: with you, and so now I speak my agitation of the matter. Therefore be

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: of good cheer, for truly I think you are damn’d. There is but one hope

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: in it that can do you any good, and that is but a kind of bastard hope

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: neither.

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: And what hope is that, I pray thee?

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: Marry, you may partly hope that your father got you not, that you are

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: not the Jew’s daughter.

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: That were a kind of bastard hope indeed; so the sins of my mother

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: should be visited upon me.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: Truly then I fear you are damn’d both by father and mother; thus when I

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: shun Scylla your father, I fall into Charybdis your mother. Well, you

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: are gone both ways.

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: I shall be saved by my husband. He hath made me a Christian.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: Truly the more to blame he, we were Christians enow before, e’en as

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: many as could well live one by another. This making of Christians will

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: raise the price of hogs; if we grow all to be pork-eaters, we shall not

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: shortly have a rasher on the coals for money.
Enter Lorenzo.

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: I’ll tell my husband, Launcelet, what you say. Here he comes.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: I shall grow jealous of you shortly, Launcelet, if you thus get my wife

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: into corners!

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: Nay, you need not fear us, Lorenzo. Launcelet and I are out. He tells

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: me flatly there’s no mercy for me in heaven, because I am a Jew’s

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: daughter; and he says you are no good member of the commonwealth, for

lines.speaker: JESSICA
lines.text: in converting Jews to Christians you raise the price of pork.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: I shall answer that better to the commonwealth than you can the getting

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: up of the negro’s belly! The Moor is with child by you, Launcelet.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: It is much that the Moor should be more than reason; but if she be less

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: than an honest woman, she is indeed more than I took her for.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: How every fool can play upon the word! I think the best grace of wit

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: will shortly turn into silence, and discourse grow commendable in none

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: only but parrots. Go in, sirrah; bid them prepare for dinner.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: That is done, sir, they have all stomachs.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Goodly Lord, what a wit-snapper are you! Then bid them prepare dinner.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: That is done too, sir, only “cover” is the word.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Will you cover, then, sir?

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: Not so, sir, neither. I know my duty.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Yet more quarrelling with occasion! Wilt thou show the whole wealth of

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: thy wit in an instant? I pray thee understand a plain man in his plain

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: meaning: go to thy fellows, bid them cover the table, serve in the

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: meat, and we will come in to dinner.

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: For the table, sir, it shall be served in; for the meat, sir, it shall

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: be covered; for your coming in to dinner, sir, why, let it be as

lines.speaker: LAUNCELET
lines.text: humours and conceits shall govern.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: O dear discretion, how his words are suited!

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: The fool hath planted in his memory

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: An army of good words, and I do know

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: A many fools that stand in better place,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Garnish’d like him, that for a tricksy word

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Defy the matter. How cheer’st thou, Jessica?

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: And now, good sweet, say thy opinion,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: How dost thou like the Lord Bassanio’s wife?

lines.speaker: JESSICA

lines.text: Empties itself, as doth an inland brook

lines.text: Into the main of waters. Music! hark!

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: It is your music, madam, of the house.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Nothing is good, I see, without respect.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Methinks it sounds much sweeter than by day.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: Silence bestows that virtue on it, madam.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: The crow doth sing as sweetly as the lark

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: When neither is attended; and I think

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: The nightingale, if she should sing by day

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: When every goose is cackling, would be thought

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: No better a musician than the wren.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: How many things by season season’d are

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: To their right praise and true perfection!

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Peace! How the moon sleeps with Endymion,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And would not be awak’d!
[_Music ceases._]

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: That is the voice,

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Or I am much deceiv’d, of Portia.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: He knows me as the blind man knows the cuckoo,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: By the bad voice.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Dear lady, welcome home.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: We have been praying for our husbands’ welfare,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Which speed, we hope, the better for our words.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Are they return’d?

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Madam, they are not yet;

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: But there is come a messenger before

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: To signify their coming.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Go in, Nerissa.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Give order to my servants, that they take

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: No note at all of our being absent hence,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Nor you, Lorenzo; Jessica, nor you.
[_A tucket sounds._]

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Your husband is at hand, I hear his trumpet.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: We are no tell-tales, madam, fear you not.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: This night methinks is but the daylight sick,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: It looks a little paler. ’Tis a day

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Such as the day is when the sun is hid.
Enter Bassanio, Antonio, Gratiano and their Followers.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: We should hold day with the Antipodes,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: If you would walk in absence of the sun.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Let me give light, but let me not be light,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: For a light wife doth make a heavy husband,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And never be Bassanio so for me.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: But God sort all! You are welcome home, my lord.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I thank you, madam. Give welcome to my friend.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: This is the man, this is Antonio,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: To whom I am so infinitely bound.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: You should in all sense be much bound to him,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: For, as I hear, he was much bound for you.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: No more than I am well acquitted of.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Sir, you are very welcome to our house.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: It must appear in other ways than words,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Therefore I scant this breathing courtesy.
[_To Nerissa_.]

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: By yonder moon I swear you do me wrong,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: In faith, I gave it to the judge’s clerk.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Would he were gelt that had it, for my part,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Since you do take it, love, so much at heart.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: A quarrel, ho, already! What’s the matter?

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: About a hoop of gold, a paltry ring

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: That she did give me, whose posy was

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: For all the world like cutlers’ poetry

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Upon a knife, “Love me, and leave me not.”

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: What talk you of the posy, or the value?

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: You swore to me when I did give it you,

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: That you would wear it till your hour of death,

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: And that it should lie with you in your grave.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: Though not for me, yet for your vehement oaths,

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: You should have been respective and have kept it.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: Gave it a judge’s clerk! No, God’s my judge,

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: The clerk will ne’er wear hair on’s face that had it.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: He will, and if he live to be a man.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: Ay, if a woman live to be a man.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Now, by this hand, I gave it to a youth,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: A kind of boy, a little scrubbed boy,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: No higher than thyself, the judge’s clerk,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: A prating boy that begg’d it as a fee,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: I could not for my heart deny it him.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: You were to blame,—I must be plain with you,—

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: To part so slightly with your wife’s first gift,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: A thing stuck on with oaths upon your finger,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And so riveted with faith unto your flesh.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I gave my love a ring, and made him swear

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Never to part with it, and here he stands.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I dare be sworn for him he would not leave it

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Nor pluck it from his finger for the wealth

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: That the world masters. Now, in faith, Gratiano,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: You give your wife too unkind a cause of grief,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: An ’twere to me I should be mad at it.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Why, I were best to cut my left hand off,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And swear I lost the ring defending it.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: My Lord Bassanio gave his ring away

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Unto the judge that begg’d it, and indeed

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Deserv’d it too. And then the boy, his clerk,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: That took some pains in writing, he begg’d mine,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: And neither man nor master would take aught

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: But the two rings.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: What ring gave you, my lord?

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Not that, I hope, which you receiv’d of me.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: If I could add a lie unto a fault,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I would deny it, but you see my finger

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Hath not the ring upon it, it is gone.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Even so void is your false heart of truth.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: By heaven, I will ne’er come in your bed

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Until I see the ring.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: Nor I in yours

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: Till I again see mine!

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Sweet Portia,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: If you did know to whom I gave the ring,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: If you did know for whom I gave the ring,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And would conceive for what I gave the ring,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And how unwillingly I left the ring,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: When nought would be accepted but the ring,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: You would abate the strength of your displeasure.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: If you had known the virtue of the ring,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Or half her worthiness that gave the ring,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Or your own honour to contain the ring,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: You would not then have parted with the ring.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: What man is there so much unreasonable,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: If you had pleas’d to have defended it

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: With any terms of zeal, wanted the modesty

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: To urge the thing held as a ceremony?

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Nerissa teaches me what to believe:

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I’ll die for’t but some woman had the ring.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: No, by my honour, madam, by my soul,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: No woman had it, but a civil doctor,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Which did refuse three thousand ducats of me,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And begg’d the ring, the which I did deny him,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And suffer’d him to go displeas’d away,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Even he that had held up the very life

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Of my dear friend. What should I say, sweet lady?

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I was enforc’d to send it after him.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I was beset with shame and courtesy.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: My honour would not let ingratitude

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: So much besmear it. Pardon me, good lady;

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: For by these blessed candles of the night,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Had you been there, I think you would have begg’d

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: The ring of me to give the worthy doctor.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Let not that doctor e’er come near my house,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Since he hath got the jewel that I loved,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And that which you did swear to keep for me,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I will become as liberal as you,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I’ll not deny him anything I have,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: No, not my body, nor my husband’s bed.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Know him I shall, I am well sure of it.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Lie not a night from home. Watch me like Argus,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: If you do not, if I be left alone,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Now by mine honour which is yet mine own,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I’ll have that doctor for mine bedfellow.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: And I his clerk. Therefore be well advis’d

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: How you do leave me to mine own protection.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Well, do you so. Let not me take him then,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: For if I do, I’ll mar the young clerk’s pen.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I am th’ unhappy subject of these quarrels.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Sir, grieve not you. You are welcome notwithstanding.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Portia, forgive me this enforced wrong,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: And in the hearing of these many friends

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I swear to thee, even by thine own fair eyes,

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Wherein I see myself—

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Mark you but that!

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: In both my eyes he doubly sees himself,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: In each eye one. Swear by your double self,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And there’s an oath of credit.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Nay, but hear me.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Pardon this fault, and by my soul I swear

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: I never more will break an oath with thee.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I once did lend my body for his wealth,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Which but for him that had your husband’s ring

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Had quite miscarried. I dare be bound again,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: My soul upon the forfeit, that your lord

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Will never more break faith advisedly.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Then you shall be his surety. Give him this,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And bid him keep it better than the other.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Here, Lord Bassanio, swear to keep this ring.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: By heaven, it is the same I gave the doctor!

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I had it of him: pardon me, Bassanio,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: For by this ring, the doctor lay with me.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: And pardon me, my gentle Gratiano,

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: For that same scrubbed boy, the doctor’s clerk,

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: In lieu of this, last night did lie with me.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Why, this is like the mending of highways

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: In summer, where the ways are fair enough.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: What, are we cuckolds ere we have deserv’d it?

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Speak not so grossly. You are all amaz’d.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Here is a letter; read it at your leisure.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: It comes from Padua from Bellario.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: There you shall find that Portia was the doctor,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Nerissa there, her clerk. Lorenzo here

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Shall witness I set forth as soon as you,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And even but now return’d. I have not yet

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Enter’d my house. Antonio, you are welcome,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And I have better news in store for you

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Than you expect: unseal this letter soon.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: There you shall find three of your argosies

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Are richly come to harbour suddenly.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: You shall not know by what strange accident

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I chanced on this letter.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I am dumb.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Were you the doctor, and I knew you not?

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Were you the clerk that is to make me cuckold?

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: Ay, but the clerk that never means to do it,

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: Unless he live until he be a man.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: Sweet doctor, you shall be my bedfellow.

lines.speaker: BASSANIO
lines.text: When I am absent, then lie with my wife.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Sweet lady, you have given me life and living;

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: For here I read for certain that my ships

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Are safely come to road.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: How now, Lorenzo!

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: My clerk hath some good comforts too for you.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: Ay, and I’ll give them him without a fee.

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: There do I give to you and Jessica,

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: From the rich Jew, a special deed of gift,

lines.speaker: NERISSA
lines.text: After his death, of all he dies possess’d of.

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Fair ladies, you drop manna in the way

lines.speaker: LORENZO
lines.text: Of starved people.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: It is almost morning,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And yet I am sure you are not satisfied

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Of these events at full. Let us go in,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And charge us there upon inter’gatories,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And we will answer all things faithfully.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Let it be so. The first inter’gatory

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: That my Nerissa shall be sworn on is,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Whether till the next night she had rather stay,

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Or go to bed now, being two hours to day.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: But were the day come, I should wish it dark

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Till I were couching with the doctor’s clerk.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Well, while I live, I’ll fear no other thing

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: So sore as keeping safe Nerissa’s ring.
[_Exeunt._]
